## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e7d02315375a18dc26e144e0623dc759b912cbff`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/eval.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/qa.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/project-forms.md + none

Inputs read: card #34632 body and all five comments (D3 correction 6938570276, ruling 6943105103, claim 6943848535 and its two amendments), PR #34745 body, file list and net diff (3 files, 10 insertions, 10 deletions, one commit on merge-base f6f5b50a05), and the check-runs on this head. The diff holds no script, gate, test or changeset, so no implementing file is in scope; `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`, `scripts/pm/mailbox-open.mjs`, `references/seat-lifecycle.md`, `references/lanes/skills.md`, `references/lanes/director.md`, pm-dispatch `SKILL.md`, and the `checklist-test` and `scenario-eval` skills were read at this head to judge the three files, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- D2 (option A), `lanes/qa.md` lines 7-8: the seat opens a round itself on three signals: a new release tag gives a smoke round, every child of an un-paused epic closed gives milestone acceptance, and one routine round a week; the maintainer can still call a round. That is D2-A item for item, and the old ban on self-starting and on building schedules is gone. Right.
- D2, release reading (line 8): the old text accepted the maintainer's word or the director seat's tag-family reading; the new text accepts only a new tag-family reading and refuses word of mouth and branch names. This narrows nothing the ruling keeps: D2-A names the release tag as the signal, and a maintainer who wants a smoke round still gets one through the call-a-round clause on the same line. Dropping the director as the producer of the reading is required for a self-started round while that seat is vacant, and reading tags is read-only. Right.
- D3 as corrected in 6938570276, `lanes/eval.md` lines 7, 13, 21, 22, 45: daily baseline, 56 questions at 5 runs each, run from the cloud against a fixed hosted test environment, gateway key kept in that environment, runner carrying persona credentials only as environment secrets, first-week real spend reported to the maintainer before any increase. Line 20, unchanged, still requires model and spend recorded every round. Every clause of the corrected D3-A is present and nothing of D3-B or D3-C survives: the per-release cadence, the no-nightly sentence, the 30 and 150 call counts and the local objectos-ee target are all removed. Right.
- D6 (option A): both charter titles name the shared verification seat and say one seat, two charters; the charters stay two files; `project-forms.md` line 14 maps the Chinese seat word for verification to `qa` plus `eval` as one seat. Right.
- Seat-word accept set (`project-forms.md` line 14): one alias added. The example list loses `server` and `objectstack`, but the rule on the same line (every file name under `lanes/` is a seat word, the directory is the whole set) is unchanged, and both files still exist under `lanes/` at this head, so no seat word stops resolving. Right.
- Other decisions: no text in the diff implements D1, D4, D5, D7, D8, D9 or R1. The one term that looked like a dependency on slice R, the un-paused epic of `qa.md` line 7, resolves at this head without it: `seat-lifecycle.md` lines 52-63 define the epic (parent card, milestone table, rolling split where the current milestone's children all closing is the milestone boundary) and its pause (`pm:on-hold` plus `Restart-when:` on the parent). No silent dependency on unlanded text.
- Names checked real at this head: `lanes/qa.md` and `lanes/eval.md`; `qa` and `eval` in `SEAT_BARE_LANES` (`scripts/pm/mailbox-open.mjs`), so `qa#N` and `eval#N` are valid seat keys; `scripts/qa/retest-owed.mjs`, `scripts/qa/qa-rollup.mjs`, `scripts/pm/fleet-roster.mjs`; the `scenario-eval` and `checklist-test` skills; the `pm:on-hold` label (SKILL.md state table). The cloud path of the baseline CLI and the question count of 56 live in the cloud repo, outside this tree; they stand on the unchanged line 12 and on the correction 6938570276 that the ruling names.
- Public surface: none. Three governed skill references; no schema, no package export, no CLI, no generated output.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no

No changeset, label `skip-changeset`, and the `Check Changeset` run on this head concluded success. That matches the diff: the three paths sit under `.claude/**`, belong to no published package, and change no behaviour a consumer can observe. `Metadata-protocol: none` is likewise correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Governed surface: all three paths are under `.claude/**`. The PR is a draft and stays a draft until the governed approver approves; Tier H is the seat's step, not this record's. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded success on this head.
- Check-runs on this head: every completed run concluded success or skipped, including `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` and the three finished type-check jobs. Four were still in progress at the time of reading and are reported as pending, not as verdicts: `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. The first of these carries the skill line ratchet and the skill id lint; the seat reads its conclusion before adopting this record, and a red there voids the line-economy paragraph of ④.
- Dev flag, definition of the un-paused epic (PR body, acceptance notes): the body says the definition lands with slice R and glosses it as an open `pm:epic` card without `pm:on-hold`. Answered from the tree: the term already resolves through `seat-lifecycle.md` lines 52-63, where the epic parent carries `tracking` and by line 54 does not carry `pm:epic`. The body's gloss is the card's R3 wording, not this tree's; `qa.md` is correct as written and the gloss is slice R's to reconcile (see N5).
- Dev flag, `lanes/skills.md` line 29 (PR body and claim amendment 6943981717): after this PR lands and until slice R lands, that line still says the QA seat's routine runs once per dev wave. Its ban on self-starting is about QA waves, which `qa.md` line 27 still leaves with the maintainer, so only the per-wave cadence goes stale. Answered: the line is the skills lane's charter, not the verification seat's; the governing text for when a round opens is `qa.md` (`checklist-test` section 6 defers to it by name), and slice R is claimed for the line. Accepted as a declared, bounded interval.
- Dev flag, `checklist-test` needs no change: confirmed. Its section 6 writes no cadence of its own and points at `lanes/qa.md`; its section 5 trigger 4 is the standing routine of section 6, which the three signals now open.
- Operational dependency of D3, escalated to the seat post and the maintainer rather than graded: the correction itself records that containers are keyless and that only the maintainer's computer has run the baseline so far. The charter is right to state the ruled target, but the first daily run needs the hosted test environment carrying the eval app and the persona secrets to exist; neither is created by this PR, and the charter no longer offers the local run as a fallback.
- `open_questions`: the PR body carries none.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff is rule text; it adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`references/lanes/qa.md`. Lines 7-8 say what D2-A decides and no more. A seat can act on each signal from text that exists at this head: the smoke round is line 13 and `checklist-test` section 6; the weekly round is the round of lines 12-21, whose first record already uses the `owed:weekly` selector; the milestone signal is the rolling-split boundary of `seat-lifecycle.md` line 56. Tried to break it against the unchanged lines: line 27 still reserves QA waves (release-candidate full runs, maintainer-named targets) for the maintainer, which does not collide with self-started routine rounds; line 14's dev-wave note describes the package mode of the scenario half, not a cadence. Holds.

`references/lanes/eval.md`. Lines 7, 13, 21, 22 and 45 carry the corrected D3 completely, and the title carries D6. Line 20 (API calls only inside the maintainer-approved budget, model and spend every round) is consistent with line 22: the runner holds no key, the hosted environment's own model calls are what bill, and the ruling is the approval for the daily 56 by 5 run. Line 19's subscription default still governs the scenario cards. The hand-off line no longer has the seat run a first baseline locally, which matches the correction's record that the first run already happened. Holds.

`references/project-forms.md`. Line 14 makes the verification word resolve to two existing lane files; lines 11 and 15 already allow one instruction line to seat several lanes and say how each lane's seat post is picked, so the summons is executable as written. Holds.

Line economy: the ratchet rows at this head are 59, 45 and 29 for `project-forms.md`, `lanes/eval.md` and `lanes/qa.md`, and the files at this head are 59, 45 and 29 lines; the diff touches no row and moves no ceiling. The ten new lines measure 71 to 119 bytes against the 120-byte cap, and the widest line in each file (120, 119, 120) is an untouched one. The gate's own verdict is the pending `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` run named in ③.

Nits, none affecting correctness or the contract; each is left for slice R or a follow-up card, since a fix here moves the head:

- N1 (nit) — `qa.md` line 7 names the milestone round acceptance but no line says what it runs. The text is still determinate: line 27 limits the seat to the section 6 routine and the scenario half, and `checklist-test` section 5 allows four retest triggers and no fifth, so a milestone signal opens an ordinary routine round. The card's target design (seat 7, lifecycle step 3) speaks of re-testing the epic's acceptance scenarios; if that is wanted it is a new rule needing its own text, and it is not part of D2.
- N2 (nit) — one seat, two charters is not carried through to the keyed artifacts. `SEAT_BARE_LANES` has `qa` and `eval` and no verification key, so the merged seat is one project holding two seat keys, two seat posts, two mailboxes and two roster rows, signing as `qa#N` or `eval#N` by charter. The tooling refuses any other key, so a wrong guess cannot land, but neither charter nor `project-forms.md` lines 23, 33 and 59 says it.
- N3 (nit) — duplication in `eval.md`: the daily cadence is stated on lines 7 and 21, and the cloud-against-hosted-environment target on lines 13 and 45. Line 45's first clause could go without losing a rule, which would also pay toward the card's net-lines target.
- N4 (nit) — `eval.md` line 7 turns the weekly scenario-card round from a suggestion into the stated cadence. That matches the card's target design for the verification seat and its two-week check, but it is not literally D2, D3 or D6; `qa.md` has no line saying how the QA half is woken, and relies on the same line's seat-owned Routines now that the two charters share a seat.
- N5 (nit) — the PR body's gloss of the un-paused epic (open `pm:epic` without `pm:on-hold`) does not match `seat-lifecycle.md` line 54, under which an epic parent carries no `pm:epic`. The tree is right; the body is a prose face and can be corrected without moving the head, and slice R should not import the gloss into `triage.md` or `filing-gate.md` without reconciling it with that line.
